defects.description: WORDPRESS_DB_HOST is set to `database`, but the database service is named `db`; there is no service or host `database`.
paraphrases: WordPress points at DB host `database`, which is not a defined service (the DB service is `db`).
The DB host should be `db`; `database` resolves to nothing.
Dangling host reference: no service named `database` exists in the file.
defects.rationale: Findable by cross-checking WORDPRESS_DB_HOST against the service names; the DB service is `db`.

defects.description: WORDPRESS_DB_NAME is `wp`, but the database created by the db service is `wordpress` (MYSQL_DATABASE=wordpress), so WordPress targets a database that does not exist.
paraphrases: WordPress looks for database `wp` but the server only creates `wordpress`.
The configured database name is inconsistent between the app and the db service.
defects.rationale: Findable by comparing WORDPRESS_DB_NAME to MYSQL_DATABASE in the same file; should be `wordpress`.

defects.description: WORDPRESS_DB_PASSWORD is `secret`, but the db user's password is `wordpress` (MYSQL_PASSWORD=wordpress), so authentication will fail.
paraphrases: The WordPress DB password differs from the password the MySQL user was created with.
App and database passwords are inconsistent, so the DB login will be rejected.
defects.rationale: Findable by comparing WORDPRESS_DB_PASSWORD to MYSQL_PASSWORD in the same file; should be `wordpress`.
